answer: One defence is a bonded trust graph: every agent occupies one vertex whose standing is backed by a locked deposit that grows only through sustained, useful work. A newcomer cannot simply whisper its way into trust, because endorsements from established vertices carry weight proportional to their own history, not their count. A sybil swarm therefore faces a real cost: each fake identity needs its own deposit, and unlike a relic account inherited or bought cheaply, a vertex with no record of delivered work earns no endorsement weight, so flooding the network buys presence but not influence.
